newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks mixed in directionless market.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks mixed in directionless market.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares were mixed on continuing profit-taking in a directionless market on Tuesday, brokers said.
"There was still some selling around and it's very difficult to say which way the market is going at the moment. It's mixed and it has no direction," one broker said.

"Probably people are now waiting to see what the rainy season is going to be like and the news about the IMF (International Monetary Fund) might be affecting trade because there are not many buyers," he added.

Michael Nowak, division chief for the IMF's Southern African Department, told reporters on Monday that Zimbabwe would not get any immediate financial aid from the fund for a new five-year economic reform programme it plans to launch later this year.

However, he said President Robert Mugabe's government might get some crucial aid in the financial year starting next July after showing progress and providing detailed plans on how it intended to curtail high state spending and a big budget deficit.

Brokers said the market had seen little impact from trade union calls for a nationwide stoppage to press the government to resolve a three-week strike by nurses and doctors which has paralysed the public health sector.

The key industrial index -- which has been sliding since last week on profit-taking -- clawed back 3.81 points to close at 7,949.45 on the back of blue-chip conglomerate Delta's 25-cent gain to 3,275.

Food and wine producer Cairns leapt 150 cents to 1,200, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans rose 100 cents to 3,700, agriculture investor Chemco gained 50 cents to 1,750 while engineering firm Gulliver added 10 cents to 200 and cement-maker Porthold put on 15 cents to 1,340.

Among the losers, construction and plastics investor IHL dropped 100 cents to 1,900, Alloys shed 50 cents to 850 while winery Afdis, glass firm PG Industries and conglomerate TA Holdings all lost 10 cents in reasonable turnover to 450, 500 and 155 respectively.
Minings continued generally flat except for Wankie Colliery which put on 10 cents to 375. Gold producer Rio Tinto dropped 100 cents to 3,500, leaving the mining index 3.57 points lower at 1,225.44.
